candidates: When a new config option gates a behavior that can occur in multiple code paths (e.g. suppressing error rendering), audit the entire function or module for every location where that behavior is triggered and apply the gate consistently — not just the first occurrence you notice.

When wrapping existing error-handling logic inside a new opt-in conditional flag, ensure that side-effects present in the original code — especially `throw` statements — are preserved in the default (flag-off) branch. Introducing a flag must never silently change the pre-existing default behavior.

In Cypress E2E tests that assert on collections of SVG elements via `.find('svg').should(($svg) => { ... })`, add per-element visibility checks (e.g. `$svg.each((_index, svg) => { expect(cy.$$(svg)).to.be.visible; })`) alongside length and content assertions to prevent race conditions where elements are present in the DOM but not yet fully rendered or visible.
